mechanism_narrative: The sharp, persistent drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the last three weeks lowers weekday trip chaining into shops and cafes, so RETAIL_REC stays below the prior four-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain near the current trough but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further week-over-week fall in TRANSIT below its current trough should cut access to central retail districts and reduce retail-and-recreation mobility within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 2 points below the t-0w level
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is already around -79% and has been near-flat at a very low level
failure_condition: If TRANSIT declines further from the current level but RETAIL_REC does not fall within the next 14 days relative to the prior two-week average, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES stay deeply negative, daytime retail demand shifts to local convenience trips rather than discretionary shopping, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above +25 and WORKPLACES stays below -70, yet RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the interaction is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in grocery-and-pharmacy trips from the current depressed level is a proxy for resumed essential errands and neighborhood circulation, which should lift retail-and-recreation mobility within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises at least 5 points from the t-0w level
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 5 points but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A relative shift of activity into PARKS can substitute for retail outings during mild-weather weekends, so a sustained park rebound should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next month.
failure_condition: If PARKS improves from the current level and RETAIL_REC rises instead of falling over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT is a stronger signal of commuting normalization than either series alone; when both move up together, retail-and-recreation mobility should increase within one week.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise from their current troughs but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility crosses from moderate restriction into a sharp rebound, it indicates enforcement slack and broader outing tolerance, which should raise retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -10 after being below -20 the prior week
failure_condition: If PARKS crosses above -10 while RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A continued divergence where RESIDENTIAL stays high and GROCERY_PHARM remains weak implies households are not substituting toward neighborhood shopping, so retail-and-recreation mobility should remain at or below its recent trough over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above +25 and GROCERY_PHARM stays below -30, but RETAIL_REC rises above the last-4-week mean within 28 days, the hypothesis fails.
